## Norfolk Southern Corp (CIK 702165) — Operating Efficiency and Profitability, FY2022–FY2024

All figures are full-year (10-K, fiscal years ended Dec 31), in USD millions. Revenue = `RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax`; operating profit = `OperatingIncomeLoss` ("income from railway operations"); expenses = `CostsAndExpenses` (railway operating expenses); net income = `NetIncomeLoss`. Ratios below are my calculations from those facts.

**Reported figures**

| Metric | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 12,745 | 12,156 | 12,123 |
| Operating expenses | 7,936 | 9,305 | 8,052 |
| Operating income | 4,809 | 2,851 | 4,071 |
| Net income | 3,270 | 1,827 | 2,622 |

**Derived ratios (my calculations)**

| Ratio | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Operating ratio (opex/revenue) | 62.3% | 76.5% | 66.4% |
| Operating margin | 37.7% | 23.5% | 33.6% |
| Net margin | 25.7% | 15.0% | 21.6% |

**What changed**

- **2023: sharp deterioration.** The operating ratio worsened by ~14.2 percentage points (62.3% → 76.5%), operating margin fell ~14.3 pp, and net margin fell ~10.6 pp. Operating income dropped 41% and net income 44% on a 5% revenue decline. The company attributes this to $1.1 billion of net expenses from the Eastern Ohio (East Palestine) incident, plus inflationary pressures, investments in operational resiliency, and higher service-related costs, partly offset by lower fuel prices (report chunk 702165/nsc-20241231:115200 and :116800).
- **2024: partial recovery.** The operating ratio improved ~10.1 pp (76.5% → 66.4%), operating margin rose ~10.1 pp, and net margin rose ~6.6 pp. Operating income rose 43% and net income 44% even though revenue was roughly flat. Management attributes the expense decline to lower net Eastern Ohio incident costs ($325M vs $1,116M), $433M of gains on railway line sales, and lower fuel prices, partly offset by $183M of restructuring charges and higher depreciation (chunks :115200, :136000, :140800).

**Caveats**
- 2024 profitability was flattered by non-recurring items: $433M of railway-line sale gains and $183M of restructuring charges. On the company's own adjusted basis, the 2024 adjusted operating ratio was 65.8% vs 67.4% in 2023 (chunk :121600), a smaller ~1.6 pp improvement than the GAAP figures suggest.
- 2023 was depressed by the one-time incident charge, so the 2024 "recovery" is largely a reversal of that rather than a clean efficiency gain; 2024's 66.4% operating ratio still remains worse than 2022's 62.3%.
- The report's own operating-ratio figures (62.3 / 76.5 / 66.4) match my calculations exactly, confirming the expense and revenue definitions align.
